newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 31.

text.p: Following were the leading stories in Sri Lankan newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Sri Lankan textile industry to get British help to survive foreign competition after multifibre agreement expires in 2005, says British Department of Trade and Industries.
Stock brokers, investors oppose five percent tax on share trading being planned by Inland Revenue Department.

Ceylon Workers Congress (CWC) union chief and cabinet minister S. Thondaman says he will not resign from government despite failure to deliver vote of plantation workers to ruling coalition. Thondaman union members voted against their CWC candidates in favour of the main opposition United National party (UNP) in recent local government poll.
EPDP leader and Jaffna district MP Douglas Devananda says two brothers of Black Tiger Anthonypillai Anton Nesarajah, now in police custody, are members of his party.

Court action to be taken against company that released untreated waste into Kelani river, from where water is supplied to capital Colombo and its suburbs, says Environment Minister Srimani Athulathmudali.
Police nabs officials taking bribes to release Tamils from detention camps in northern Vavuniya.
S. Thondaman alleges UNP used a letter with his forged signature to get members of his CWC plantation union to vote for it in recent local government poll.
